latestRelease.notes:
## Release Notes

Released on 2026-08-14.

### Python

- Add CPython 3.10.21, 3.11.16, and 3.12.14 ([#21138](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21138))
- Prefer newer versions and standard variants when selecting between equally prioritized Python interpreters ([#21134](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21134))

### Enhancements

- Simplify errors and hints for invalid editable requirements, and redact credentials in requirement URLs ([#21130](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21130))

### Preview features

- Allow `--index` and `--default-index` to select configured package indexes by name with the `index-by-name` preview feature ([#17455](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/17455))
- Include distribution artifact URLs and hashes in CycloneDX SBOM exports by default ([#21131](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21131))
- Fall back to logical file sizes when using `cache-physical-space` on filesystems that do not support physical-space accounting ([#21133](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21133))

### Bug fixes

- Resolve relative package index paths in PEP 723 scripts against the script directory ([#21097](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21097))

## Install uv 0.12.5

### Install prebuilt binaries via shell script

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.12.5/uv-installer.sh | sh
```

### Install prebuilt binaries via powershell script

```sh
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.12.5/uv-installer.ps1 | iex"
```

## Verifying GitHub Artifact Attestations

The artifacts in this release have attestations generated with GitHub Artifact Attestations. These can be verified by using the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify):
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --repo astral-sh/uv
```

You can also download the attestation from [GitHub](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/attestations) and verify against that directly:
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --bundle <file-path of downloaded attestation>
```

signals.title: Error reading requirements.txt
signals.text: Hello there, I wanted to install the requirements for a well known [github project](https://github.com/pymedusa/Medusa/blob/master/requirements.txt), but I got this error : ``` $ uv pip install --break-system-packages --system -r requirements.txt error: Couldn't parse requirement in `requirements.txt` at position 0 Caused by: Expected direct URL (`https://codeload.github.com/pymedusa/adba/tar.gz/37b0c74e76b40b3dbde29e71da75a1808eb121de`) to end in a supported file extension: `.whl`, `.tar.gz`, `.zip`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.lz`, `.tar.lzma`, `.tar.xz`, `.tar.zst`, `.tar`, `.tbz`, `.tgz`, `.tlz`, or `.txz` adba @ https://codeload.github.com/pymedusa/adba/tar.gz/37b0c74e76b40b3dbde29e71da75a1808eb121de ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ``` Here are my questions : a) is there some sort of flag to disable url checking ? b) if not, I think that's a bug : we should be able to download a GZIP file, without checking the end of the URL for a whitelist (`.whl`, `.tar.gz`, `.zip`, etc) Also if this is some sort of security, please note that the end of the URL (ie. the extension )means nothing, the server could send us anything. Thank you :) Additional informations: - OS : alpine linux v3.21.0 - python : 3.12.8 - uv : 0.5.13
signals.author: ojio-san

signals.title: Make uv tool upgrade --all tolerant to deleted Python versions
signals.text: ### Summary This is partly a follow up to some of the commentary on https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/8067 I found if I deleted a uv python version (in this case because I'd installed Python 3.13.2 with uv), e.g. ```shell uv python uninstall cpython-3.13.1-windows-x86_64-none ``` and that was the Python my uv tools were installed against, when I run: ```shell uv tool upgrade --all ``` I get a long list of errors, e.g. ```shell error: Failed to upgrade hatch Caused by: `hatch` is missing a valid environment; run `uv tool install --force hatch` to reinstall error: Failed to upgrade linkchecker Caused by: `linkchecker` is missing a valid environment; run `uv tool install --force linkchecker` to reinstall error: Failed to upgrade maturin Caused by: `maturin` is missing a valid environment; run `uv tool install --force maturin` to reinstall error: Failed to upgrade mkdocs Caused by: `mkdocs` is missing a valid environment; run `uv tool install --force mkdocs` to reinstall ``` My only options (I'm aware of) to get around this are to: 1. For each tool call `uv tool install --force <tool name>` as suggested (but I have dozens of tools and that's onerous). 2. Reinstall the Python I deleted `uv python install cpython-3.13.1-windows-x86_64-none`, then run `uv tool upgrade --all --python 3.13.2`, then uninstall the older Python after the upgrade `uv python install cpython-3.13.1-windows-x86_64-none` - which is easy when you understand the workflow but not obvious and for me required searching uv documentation / issues I was hoping the behaviour of `uv tool upgrade --all` could be changed to do a force reinstall itself in the situation the previous Python it was installed against was removed - or there could be some new CLI options, e.g. `uv tool upgrade --all --force` or `uv tool reinstall --all` - something like that where I could express I do want to force reinstall everything in the case I know I have deleted the Python the tool was installed with. I guess a related bit of feature parity it'd be nice to have versus pipx is `pipx list` shows the Python version each package was installed with whereas `uv tool list` doesn't show that. My current uv version is: `uv 0.6.0 (591f38c25 2025-02-14)`
signals.author: owenlamont

signals.title: uv tool install: "--reinstall" option broken
signals.text: ### Summary `uv tool install --help` shows an option `--reinstall` to reinstall _all_ packages. However, this option requires a single package: ```bash ❯ uv tool install --help | grep -- --reinstall --reinstall Reinstall all packages, regardless of whether they're already installed. Implies `--refresh` --reinstall-package <REINSTALL_PACKAGE> Reinstall a specific package, regardless of whether it's already installed. Implies ❯ uv tool install --reinstall error: the following required arguments were not provided: <PACKAGE> Usage: uv.exe tool install --reinstall <PACKAGE> For more information, try '--help'. ``` Use case: trying to "fix" installation after removing the version of python they were installed with. (No warning or error was given during `uv python uninstall 3.13.2`.) See also #14814, which speaks to more of conflicting information about this use case. ### Platform Windows version: 10.0.26200.5722, arm64 ### Version uv 0.8.4 (e176e1714 2025-07-30) ### Python version ❯ uv python list | grep -v available > cpython-3.13.3-windows-aarch64-none C:\Users\hwine\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313-arm64\python.exe > cpython-3.10.16-windows-x86_64-none C:\Users\hwine\AppData\Roaming\uv\python\cpython-3.10.16-windows-x86_64-none\python.exe
signals.author: hwine

signals.title: Too strict PEP508 validation for URLs without file extension
signals.text: ### Summary Hi, package pyro-api contains following URL in test dependencies (extra_requires): ``` pyro-ppl@https://api.github.com/repos/pyro-ppl/pyro/tarball/dev ``` See https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro-api/blob/0.1.2/setup.py I know the comment in setup.py says to remove these lines before uploading to PyPI, however I don't think this comment is correct. The above URL is fine, can be downloaded (creates a tar.gz file) and satisfies the PEP508 grammar (I checked it using code like at https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/8326#issuecomment-2423123210_) Note: I don't want to discuss if it makes sense to provide a non-pinned, no-hash, mutable URL as a requirement. After building a wheel pyro-abi 0.1.2 directly from the source code (without commenting out the test extras), I can install the resulting wheel using 'pip'. However, installation with uv fails: ``` × Failed to read `pyro-api @ file:///tmp/pyro_api-0.1.2-py3-none-any.whl` ├─▶ Couldn't parse metadata of pyro_api-0.1.2-py3-none-any.whl from pyro-api @ file:///work/lbuild-out/pyro_api-0.1.2-py3-none-any.whl ╰─▶ Expected direct URL (`https://api.github.com/repos/pyro-ppl/pyro/tarball/dev`) to end in a supported file extension: `.whl`, `.tar.gz`, `.zip`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.lz`, `.tar.lzma`, `.tar.xz`, `.tar.zst`, `.tar`, `.tbz`, `.tgz`, `.tlz`, or `.txz` pyro-ppl@ https://api.github.com/repos/pyro-ppl/pyro/tarball/dev ; extra == "test" ``` I believe the requirement of the file extension is too strict and not justified by PEP508 (or PEP 440). My expectation is that `pyro-ppl@https://api.github.com/repos/pyro-ppl/pyro/tarball/dev` should be accepted as a proper requirement URL. ### Platform Linux 6.10.14-linuxkit aarch64 GNU/Linux ### Version uv 0.9.22 (82a6a66b8 2026-01-06) ### Python version 3.13.8
signals.author: ppalucha

signals.title: Alternatives for handling issues with `uv lock [--check]` and `exclude-newer`
signals.text: ### Summary We create the `uv.lock` files for our client projects on our Mac workstations. The projects run containerized in both dev and prod machines. We're planning on instituting a company-wide 7-day cooldown period in all of our global package manager configurations on our workstations. In preparation for this, I was experimenting with `exclude-newer` in my global `uv.toml`, but this caused a container build failure after a subsequent lockfile update. To ensure that the lockfile is up to date with `pyproject.toml` during the container build, in `Dockerfile`, we've got an early `uv lock --check` command (and a later install with `uv sync --locked`, ensuring no lockfile changes are attempted by the build process). If the lockfile check fails, we'll manually update it on the host and then retry the container build. The error in the build process is this: ``` $ uv lock --check Using CPython 3.14.3 interpreter at: /usr/local/bin/python3 Resolving despite existing lockfile due to removal of global exclude newer Resolved 70 packages in 1.64s The lockfile at `uv.lock` needs to be updated, but `--check` was provided. To update the lockfile, run `uv lock`. ``` The lockfile is up to date as far as the packages are concerned. Seemingly `--check` doesn't like these two lines that the host-level locking created, since the container doesn't have `exclude-newer` configured. ``` [options] exclude-newer = "2026-03-24T09:21:26.001329Z" exclude-newer-span = "P7D" ``` I guess the question is, is this `exclude-newer` configuration mismatch so serious that it should unconditionally fail the lockfile check? For us, it's certainly not. There are various ways to approach this, including but not limited to the following: - An option like `--check-packages-only` for `uv lock`, deliberately only caring about the locked packages matching `pyproject.toml`, not `exclude-newer` or other similar non-package-version-related mismatches. - A specific option for `--check` to ignore the `exclude-newer` mismatch. - No change; always require `exclude-newer` in `pyproject.toml` if host/container consistency is needed. ---- What to do when encountering an existing lockfile/config mismatch is one thing, but could this perhaps be caught earlier, at the time when the options would get baked into the lockfile in the first place? Consider this scenario: a project doesn't have `exclude-newer` in `pyproject.toml`, deliberately or not. A new contributor has `exclude-newer` globally set and runs `uv lock` to add a dependency, baking the options to the lockfile, possibly to the consternation of other developers down the line without `exclude-newer` set who have to deal with testing the PR or resultant CI failures if `uv lock --check` is involved. Perhaps a global-only config could be handled specially to avoid problems like this? If the lockfile doesn't already contain `exclude-newer` options AND the option is only set globally by the user running `uv lock`, not in `pyproject.toml` for the project being locked nor specified with `--exclude-newer[-package]`, pick one of these options: a) Warn the user, refuse to lock the file, require specifying an option that tells uv whether to bake the options in. b) Prompt the user about what to do, offering to lock with or without baking the options in. Likewise, if the lockfile already does contain `exclude-newer`, but `pyproject.toml` for some reason doesn't, it would probably be clearest to not change the baked-in values if they differ from the locking user's global setting only. I'm sure there are backwards compatibility considerations here, but I feel like uv needs a somewhat "clearer story" around globally set `exclude-newer`. With supply chain attacks happening regularly, articles around the web increasingly recommend global package manager configs for cooldowns, so the current behavior is bound to cause surprises for people down the line. ### Example _No response_
signals.author: jklaiho

signals.title: `uv sync --frozen` ignores all index/mirror configuration and uses hardcoded URLs from `uv.lock`
signals.text: # Bug Report: `uv sync --frozen` ignores all index/mirror configuration and uses hardcoded URLs from `uv.lock` ## Environment - **uv version**: 0.11.14 (in Dify plugin daemon) & 0.11.17 (latest, locally tested) - **Platform**: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, x86_64) / macOS (Darwin 15.6.1, arm64) - **Python**: 3.12+ (tested with 3.12 and 3.13) ## Description When running `uv sync --frozen --no-dev`, **all index/mirror configuration methods are completely ignored**. uv downloads packages directly from the hardcoded URLs stored in `uv.lock` (typically `https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/...`), regardless of: - Command-line flag: `-i https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/` - Environment variable: `UV_INDEX_URL` - Environment variable: `UV_DEFAULT_INDEX` - Config file: `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` (`[[index]]` section) - Config file: `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` (`[pip]` section) - Project config: `pyproject.toml` (`[[tool.uv.index]]` section) **In contrast**, running `uv sync` **without** `--frozen` correctly respects the mirror configuration. This is a critical issue for users in regions where `files.pythonhosted.org` is slow or inaccessible (e.g., China), as well as for enterprise environments using private PyPI mirrors. ## Steps to Reproduce ```bash # 1. Create a test project mkdir -p /tmp/uv-frozen-bug && cd /tmp/uv-frozen-bug cat > pyproject.toml << 'EOF' [project] name = "frozen-mirror-test" version = "0.0.1" requires-python = ">=3.12" dependencies = [ "pydantic>=2.0", "requests>=2.31", "rich>=13.0", ] EOF # 2. Generate lockfile (this will use default pypi.org -> pythonhosted URLs) uv sync # 3. Verify uv.lock contains hardcoded pythonhosted URLs grep -c "files.pythonhosted.org" uv.lock # Output: 155 (or similar number of hardcoded URLs) # 4. Clean venv to force re-download rm -rf .venv # 5. Try frozen sync WITH mirror config (verbose to see actual URLs) UV_INDEX_URL=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/ \ uv sync --frozen --no-dev -v 2>&1 | grep -E "(aliyun|pythonhosted|Downloading)" # EXPECTED: Downloading from mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/... # ACTUAL: Downloading from files.pythonhosted.org/packages/c1/81/...pydantic_core... # Downloading from files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f4/7e/...pygments... # Downloading from files.pythonhosted.org/packages/82/3b/...rich... # 6. For comparison: try WITHOUT --frozen (same mirror config) rm -rf .venv UV_INDEX_URL=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/ \ uv sync --no-dev -v 2>&1 | grep -E "(aliyun|pythonhosted|Using index|Resolved)" # RESULT: Uses mirrors.aliyun.com correctly! ✅ ``` ## Expected Behavior `--frozen` should **freeze dependency versions** (which it does correctly), but should still use the configured **download source/index URL** for fetching packages. Version locking and download source are two separate concerns. Expected output: ``` Resolved from index at: https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/ Downloading https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/packages/...pydantic_core... ``` ## Actual Behavior ``` # All 7 configuration methods are ignored: DEBUG Resolved 155 packages in Xms Downloading https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/c1/81/...pydantic_core-2.30.0-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.manylinux2014_x86_64.whl Downloading https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f4/7e/...pygments-2.19.0-py3-none-any.whl Downloading https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/82/3b/...rich-13.9.4-py3-none-any.whl # ... all from pythonhosted, completely ignoring UV_INDEX_URL ``` ## Comparison Table | Mode | Mirror Config Set | Actual Download Source | Result | |------|-------------------|----------------------|--------| | `uv sync --no-dev` | `UV_INDEX_URL=aliyun` | `mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/...` | ✅ Works | | `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` | `UV_INDEX_URL=aliyun` | `files.pythonhosted.org/packages/...` | ❌ Ignored | ## Real-World Impact This bug caused **6 failed installation attempts** of a Python plugin in our production environment (Dify AI platform on a 2C4G cloud server in China): 1. Plugin daemon calls `uv sync --no-dev --frozen` internally 2. All dependencies download from `files.pythonhosted.org` at ~10 KB/s (vs ~10 MB/s from Chinese mirrors) 3. Download timeout after 300s → `signal: terminated` → installation failure 4. Server has limited RAM (4GB) + swap, so slow downloads also risk OOM during dependency building **Workaround used**: Replaced `/usr/local/bin/uv` with a bash wrapper that intercepts `uv sync` calls and redirects them to `pip3 install -i <mirror-url>`. ```bash #!/bin/bash # /usr/local/bin/uv (wrapper script) if [[ "$1" == "sync" ]]; then echo "[wrapper] Intercepted uv sync -> using pip3 with aliyun mirror" >&2 # Create venv with pip, install deps via pip3 -i <mirror> python3 -m venv .venv DEPS=$(python3 -c "import tomllib; ...") echo "$DEPS" | .venv/bin/pip3 install -i "$INDEX_URL" -r /dev/stdin exit $? else exec /usr/local/bin/uv-real "$@" fi ``` ## Suggested Fix Direction The `--frozen` flag's purpose is to **lock dependency versions**, not to **lock download URLs**. The fix should: 1. Read package versions and hashes from `uv.lock` (current behavior — correct) 2. Resolve the **actual download URL** using the configured index/mirror (new behavior) 3. Only fall back to the lockfile's hardcoded URL if the configured index doesn't have the matching package+version+hash This is similar to how Cargo/Rust handles `.lock` files: versions are locked, but registries can be configured independently. ## Related Issues - **#6349** — Feature request for `uv.lock` to support different index URLs across machines/CI environments. This bug is essentially the **runtime manifestation** of that design limitation. - **#16996** — `--frozen` silently ignores resolution options (different scope, same pattern of silent ignoring) ## Additional Notes - The `uv.lock` format stores per-package download URLs like: ```toml wheels = [{ url = "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/...", hash = "sha256:..." }] ``` These URLs are resolved at lockfile generation time and baked in permanently. - In `--frozen` mode, uv appears to use these stored URLs directly without consulting any runtime index configuration. - Tested on both **0.11.14** (Dify's pinned version) and **0.11.17** (latest release as of 2025-05-28). Behavior is identical — this is not version-specific.
signals.author: chenshengtao666

signals.title: uv-build: suppress "missing upper bound" warning via env var
signals.text: ### Summary I frequently work with Python projects where uv is locked by [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/). A dummy project with mise + uv + configuration scaffolding is [here](https://github.com/manselmi/yospos). Given that 1. [mise locks the uv version](https://github.com/manselmi/yospos/blob/019a251385da23e3ad74254141e156d627ae4074/mise.lock#L22-L42), and 2. given my understanding (which might very well be wrong) that commands such as `uv build` and `uv sync` use a build backend embedded in the `uv` binary, which I assume doesn't need to download the `uv-build` Python package (again, this might be wrong), it seems like it should be safe to omit an upper bound (or any sort of version constraint) for `uv-build` in `build-system.requires` in `pyproject.toml` ([example](https://github.com/manselmi/yospos/blob/019a251385da23e3ad74254141e156d627ae4074/pyproject.toml#L8)). However, as far as I know, there is no way to suppress the following warning without specifying an upper bound on `uv-build`: ``` text warning: `build_system.requires = ["uv-build"]` is missing an upper bound on the `uv_build` version such as `<0.13`. Without bounding the `uv_build` version, the source distribution will break when a future, breaking version of `uv_build` is released. ``` I would like to be able to suppress this warning, perhaps via environment variable, in situations where uv is pinned. If uv is pinned then the warning is effectively a false-positive, and the alert should be suppressible to reduce alert fatigue. Also, in this situation it makes sense to specify a `uv`/`uv-build` version constraint in only one place, `mise.toml`, and not in both `mise.toml` and `pyproject.toml`, yet another reason for making the warning suppressible. ``` console % uv --version uv 0.12.3 (Homebrew 2026-08-07 aarch64-apple-darwin) ``` ### Example #### Current behavior Warning emitted, as there's no way to suppress the `uv-build` upper bound warning without supplying an upper bound. First, clone https://github.com/manselmi/yospos/ then run ``` console % mise exec -- uv build --wheel Building wheel... warning: `build_system.requires = ["uv-build"]` is missing an upper bound on the `uv_build` version such as `<0.13`. Without bounding the `uv_build` version, the source distribution will break when a future, breaking version of `uv_build` is released. ``` (The example project only supports Linux and macOS but you get the idea.) #### Desired behavior Warning suppressed when some environment variable is truthy. `UV_NO_BUILD_UPPER_BOUND_WARNING` is used in the following example, although that's a mouthful. ``` console % env -- UV_NO_BUILD_UPPER_BOUND_WARNING=1 mise exec -- uv build --wheel Building wheel... ``` In practice, this environment variable would be set in a project-specific `mise.toml` configuration file so that it doesn't need to be manually set.
signals.author: manselmi

signals.title: `uv run` uses wrong python interpreter inside virtualenv with copied python
signals.text: ### Summary I tried using uv with an old project that creates its own venv using a python version that isn't the system deafult python. The system default /usr/bin/python3, used by default by uv, is python3.9 ```sh % uv run python --version Python 3.9.25 ``` `uv run --with some_dependency` breaks inside venvs that use a different python. Minimal reproduction: ```sh % cd `mktemp -d` % python3.13 <<< 'import venv ; venv.create(".venv")' % . .venv/bin/activate % uv run --with ipython ipython Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/mneergaa/.cache/uv/builds-v0/.tmpfB0eqd/bin/ipython", line 4, in <module> from IPython import start_ipython ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'IPython' ``` Interestingly, it works if I use `python3 -m venv` to create the venv, probably because that uses symlinks instead of copying: ```sh % cd `mktemp -d` % python3.13 -m venv .venv % . .venv/bin/activate % uv run --with ipython ipython Python 3.13.14 (main, Jun 11 2026, 00:00:00) [GCC 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-14)] [...] ``` ### Platform CentOS Stream release 9 ### Version uv 0.12.2 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) ### Python version Python 3.9.25 / Python 3.13.14

signals.title: `uv check --script` ignores `exclude-newer-package` exemptions when selecting `ty`
signals.text: ### Summary ## Summary `uv check --script` applies the global `exclude-newer` cutoff when selecting ty, even when ty is explicitly exempted with `exclude-newer-package = { ty = false }`. ## Reproduction `pyproject.toml`: ```toml [project] name = "example" version = "0.1.0" requires-python = ">=3.12" [tool.uv] package = false exclude-newer = "P7D" exclude-newer-package = { ty = false } ``` `script.py`: ```python # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.12" # dependencies = [] # # [tool.uv] # exclude-newer = "P7D" # exclude-newer-package = { ty = false } # /// value: int = 1 ``` ```console $ uvx --no-config ty@latest --version ty 0.0.73 (4bd2833c4 2026-08-18) $ uv check --script script.py --show-version --preview-features=check-command Using ty 0.0.70 All checks passed! ``` ## Expected behavior `uv check --script` respects the ty-specific exemption and selects ty 0.0.73. ## Actual behavior `uv check --script` ignores the exemption and selects ty 0.0.70. ## Likely cause `crates/uv/src/commands/project/check.rs` passes only the global cutoff to the ty resolver: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/76d653943c6c82d3cca03227c24e98b1d0320aed/crates/uv/src/commands/project/check.rs#L721-L725 Package-specific overrides are discarded. ### Platform aarch64-apple-darwin ### Version uv 0.12.5 (210d1f678 2026-08-14) ### Python version _No response_
signals.author: AlexWaygood

signals.title: Index username stripped from url in `uv-receipt.toml` preventing tool upgrades
signals.text: ### Summary When you install a tool from a private index whose URL has a username value but no password in it, the resulting `uv-receipt.toml` has a stripped version of the URL without the username. This causes `uv tool upgrade <toolname>` to silently fail. You have to instead re-provide the index with the username like `uv tool upgrade <toolname> --index https://user@private.index/simple`. Reproducible with a uv.toml such as: ```toml # Add our private python registry index-url = "https://user@private.index/simple/" keychain-provider = "subprocess" ``` Install a tool from the private index: `uv tool install tool-name`. This provides a `uv-receipt.toml` like: ```toml [tool] requirements = [{ name = "tool-name" }] entrypoints = [ { name = "tool-name", install-path = "/Users/cole/.local/bin/tool-name", from = "tool-name" }, ] [tool.options] index-url = "https://private.index/simple/" keyring-provider = "subprocess" ``` Then if you run `uv tool upgrade tool-name` you always get: ``` $ uv tool upgrade saltfab Nothing to upgrade ``` Even when there is an upgrade available. signals.text: The `--no-build` help says resolving will not run arbitrary Python code and operations that require building distributions will fail. This conflicts with `docs/pip/compatibility.md` and the implementation: `--no-build` aliases `--only-binary :all:`, but uv may still build editable requirements under either option, and their build backends may execute arbitrary Python code. This PR updates the help text to align with reality and the doc mentioned above.

signals.title: Only warn about unbounded build backends for source distributions
signals.text: An unbounded `uv_build` requirement currently triggers a warning while building wheels, editable wheels, and metadata even though those artifacts do not distribute build-system requirements. Restrict the missing-upper-bound warning to source-distribution build. I think our warning here is a bit overzealous for people who do not intend to distribute a source distribution, so I think we should scope the warning to the case we're focused on. For example, `uv sync` and `uv build --wheel` will no longer emit the warning. Closes astral-sh/uv#21074

signals.title: Reimplement `package.metadata`-less lockfiles
signals.text: The previous iterations of `package.metadata`-free lockfiles had missed a number of cases, and made it hard to ensure that all cases were actually covered. This PR takes a new approach: Remove the previous implementation, and then re-add it feature-by-feature in reviewable commit units. Each commit adds one feature that uv supports. The new approach is not entirely `package.metadata`-free, instead remote URL, which can activate other URL source, now have `package.metadata` which they previously didn't. That's required for offline validation (which is crucial for `uv lock --check` performance, offline or not) and IMO the more correct tradeoff: We shouldn't repeat information that's already available on disk, but we should state what we expect from remote resources. This is a lockfile size regression if you're using a lot of remote URLs, otherwise it's still a much smaller lockfile for large workspaces. Remote source are usually used sparingly as they are worse for performance, reliability and auditability than registry sources. ## Validation This change reflects basically every resolver assumption and form of dependency specification and also hits a number of preexisting bugs (see upstack PRs and skipped changes list). Instead of trying to reason through correctness from the features we're representing, this PR was tested (and fixed) against large, diverse validation set, checking that uv's invariants are upheld with lockfile revision 1.4. The PR is additionally split into one commit per feature the new freshness check support, to ease reviewing and ensure that all features are covered. The most import check that needs to always pass is `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` on a fresh lockfile. We don't need to check features such as `uv sync`, as `package.metadata` is only used for fast path freshness checks, and `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` exercises the offline fast path while blocking the slow path if it would use the internet (which is unacceptable both for performance and for checks that run in isolated environments). The goal is to cover the available dependency specification that people use, while not fixing unrelated bugs in this already large change. There are three of these larger validations. The first one is a script finds public GitHub projects with editable packages, workspaces, Git dependencies or dynamically generated dependencies and then verifies that both the original lockfile and a version with package metadata removed pass `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` inside an isolated docker container. This dataset contained 254 projects with 14k locked packages. The second validation uses the check-mode in https://github.com/astral-sh/uv-ecosystem-testing with `UV_PREVIEW_FEATURES=lock-without-metadata` . The third one is running the test suite migrated to lockfile revision 1.4 with https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/commit/4b98802626b18406a47e71fc2583bc5576934e6e, passing 4.8k tests: ``` features=test-python-patch,test-universal,native-auth cargo insta test --accept --test-runner nextest --workspace --features "$features" cargo nextest run --workspace --features "$features" ``` The PR handles the test cases and fixes from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/20803 too. ## Skipped changes The following independent bugfixes are deliberately excluded from this stack: - #21210. - #21225. The cache assertion remains a TODO here. The 4.8k-test run above included the add-cache fix and predates this extraction; it is not a fresh full-suite run of the reduced stack.

signals.title: Lock Prettier tooling and disable install scripts
signals.text: The formatting workflow, contributor commands, generators, and editor hook fetch Prettier through one-shot `npx` invocations without a committed lockfile. Add a shared private `npm` toolchain that locks the existing `3.9.0` formatter and the README generator's `3.8.3` release, and disable lifecycle scripts in `.npmrc`. Require `npm>=11.10.0` through `engines.npm` and `engine-strict` so older installers cannot silently ignore the seven-day `min-release-age` policy for new resolutions. CI pins Node.js to `24.19.0`, and CI and release preparation install the tools with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. Callers then run the installed CLI directly so formatting cannot fall back to a download. Keep the root tooling lock under Renovate's shared update policy. Related: astral-sh/uv#21197 removes uv's contributor hook configuration. astral-sh/uv#21204 separately moves Python-tool invocations into the locked `check` group. astral-sh/ruff#27842 hardens the native `prek` formatter environment, while astral-sh/hawk#161 records a locked `npm` formatter environment.

signals.title: Preserve transitive self-constraints in recursive extras
signals.text: uv currently loses recursive self-constraints: If `project[outer]` includes `project[middle]`, and the `middle` extra requires `project[inner]>=2`, uv must honor the `>=2` requirement and not accept `project==1`. To do this, we keep recursive requirement around instead of discarding it. Related to #21181.
signals.author: konstin

signals.title: Reuse direct URL wheels across hash fragments
signals.text: Direct wheel requirements can include hash fragments, but lockfiles store the fragment-free URL. Using the original requirement URL as the wheel cache key can therefore prevent an offline sync from reusing an already-downloaded wheel. Use the fragment-free location for new cache entries and retain a fallback for older fragment-bearing entries. Check the expected hashes, size, and archive existence before reuse. When online, refresh a cached direct wheel if its contents no longer match the required hash or size, even when its HTTP response is still fresh. The regression tests cover offline reuse from lockfiles, offline hash mismatches, and changed contents at the same URL.

signals.title: Use the versions bot's ruleset bypass when merging
signals.text: ## Summary Use `gh pr merge --squash --admin` when merging the versions bot's release-manifest PR. The `versions` ruleset requires human review but grants `astral-versions-bot` a pull-request-only bypass. signals.title: Verify locked source archives before building metadata
signals.text: `uv.lock` records trusted archive digests, but existing-lock validation and fresh locked resolution can obtain source metadata without enforcing those digests. A replaced source distribution can therefore execute its PEP 517 build backend with the invoking developer's or CI runner's authority before a later hash or lockfile check rejects it. Registry sources are affected too, even when the index continues to advertise the original hash. Direct URLs ending in `#subdirectory=.` can also lose their trusted hash when the source identity is reconstructed. Keep hash generation and verification as independent parts of `HashStrategy`. Locked resolution verifies known registry artifacts and direct-URL source archives while preserving normal hash generation for other distributions. Normalize equivalent archive subdirectories before looking up trusted hashes, and require cached source metadata to satisfy the same policy. Stream source archives into temporary directories, then verify their complete archive hashes before publishing the source tree to the cache or using it for metadata and builds. Cache repair also checks the previous revision's digests before restoring its source tree. Ordinary sync remains protected when it reuses a lockfile, while explicitly requested unlocked updates can replace recorded hashes.
signals.author: astral-automations-bot[bot]

signals.title: Ensure full Git commit pins resolve to the requested commit
signals.text: uv treats an arbitrary Git `rev` as a potentially ambiguous branch, tag, or commit, even when the revision is a full 40-character commit SHA. On a Git server that accepts SHA-shaped branch names, a repository owner can create a branch named after an audited commit but point it at different content. A fresh install or lock operation can then select that branch before the requested object, execute the substituted package or build backend, and record the attacker-selected commit in `uv.lock` despite the supposedly immutable pin. Related inconsistencies can also enter through a locked Git URL, a PEP 751 `requested-revision` and `commit-id`, or cached Git preferences. Resolve full hexadecimal revisions through the existing exact-object fetch path instead of searching branches and tags. Reject disagreements between an exact requested revision and its precise commit when parsing Git URLs and `uv.lock` sources, when consuming PEP 751 lockfiles during installation or compilation, and before reusing or fetching a cached Git checkout. Preserve abbreviated hexadecimal references, explicitly selected branches and tags, case-insensitive commit matching, and credential-redacted error messages.

signals.title: Include build dependencies in uv pip compile
signals.text: ## Summary Prior to this change, `uv pip compile --generate-hashes` omitted isolated build dependencies and allowed both wheel and source hashes, leaving backend requirements outside the compiled dependency set and permitting source builds when a compatible wheel was available. Add an opt-in `--include-build-dependencies` mode, also configurable through `[tool.uv.pip]`, that discovers declared and dynamic PEP 517 build requirements for selected source distributions, recursively resolves their closure alongside runtime dependencies, and preserves applicable build constraints. The behavior is covered by the `include-build-dependencies` preview feature. When generating hashes, retain only compatible wheel hashes when a wheel is selected and only the source hash when a source build is required. Version selection remains unchanged, so a newer source distribution is still preferred over an older wheel. ```console $ uv pip compile requirements.in --include-build-dependencies --generate-hashes --preview-features include-build-dependencies -o requirements.txt $ uv pip install -r requirements.txt --require-hashes --build-constraint requirements.txt --preview-features build-constraint-hashes ``` The separate `build-constraint-hashes` preview feature makes `uv pip install` and `uv pip sync` require hashes for isolated build dependencies when build constraints contain hashes. Without that preview feature, or when build constraints contain no hashes, existing behavior is unchanged. Universal and `pylock.toml` output remain unsupported because the build closure is environment-specific.

signal.title: Reimplement `package.metadata`-less lockfiles
signal.text: The previous iterations of `package.metadata`-free lockfiles had missed a number of cases, and made it hard to ensure that all cases were actually covered. This PR takes a new approach: Remove the previous implementation, and then re-add it feature-by-feature in reviewable commit units. Each commit adds one feature that uv supports. The new approach is not entirely `package.metadata`-free, instead remote URL, which can activate other URL source, now have `package.metadata` which they previously didn't. That's required for offline validation (which is crucial for `uv lock --check` performance, offline or not) and IMO the more correct tradeoff: We shouldn't repeat information that's already available on disk, but we should state what we expect from remote resources. This is a lockfile size regression if you're using a lot of remote URLs, otherwise it's still a much smaller lockfile for large workspaces. Remote source are usually used sparingly as they are worse for performance, reliability and auditability than registry sources. ## Validation This change reflects basically every resolver assumption and form of dependency specification and also hits a number of preexisting bugs (see upstack PRs and skipped changes list). Instead of trying to reason through correctness from the features we're representing, this PR was tested (and fixed) against large, diverse validation set, checking that uv's invariants are upheld with lockfile revision 1.4. The PR is additionally split into one commit per feature the new freshness check support, to ease reviewing and ensure that all features are covered. The most import check that needs to always pass is `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` on a fresh lockfile. We don't need to check features such as `uv sync`, as `package.metadata` is only used for fast path freshness checks, and `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` exercises the offline fast path while blocking the slow path if it would use the internet (which is unacceptable both for performance and for checks that run in isolated environments). The goal is to cover the available dependency specification that people use, while not fixing unrelated bugs in this already large change. There are three of these larger validations. The first one is a script finds public GitHub projects with editable packages, workspaces, Git dependencies or dynamically generated dependencies and then verifies that both the original lockfile and a version with package metadata removed pass `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` inside an isolated docker container. This dataset contained 254 projects with 14k locked packages. The second validation uses the check-mode in https://github.com/astral-sh/uv-ecosystem-testing with `UV_PREVIEW_FEATURES=lock-without-metadata` . The third one is running the test suite migrated to lockfile revision 1.4 with https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/commit/4b98802626b18406a47e71fc2583bc5576934e6e, passing 4.8k tests: ``` features=test-python-patch,test-universal,native-auth cargo insta test --accept --test-runner nextest --workspace --features "$features" cargo nextest run --workspace --features "$features" ``` The PR handles the test cases and fixes from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/20803 too. ## Skipped changes The following independent bugfixes are deliberately excluded from this stack: - #21210. - #21225. The cache assertion remains a TODO here. The 4.8k-test run above included the add-cache fix and predates this extraction; it is not a fresh full-suite run of the reduced stack.

signal.title: Respect package-specific cutoffs when selecting `ty`
signal.text: `uv check` discarded package-specific `exclude-newer` settings when selecting its standalone `ty` binary, so an exemption or date override could still be constrained by the global cutoff. Use the effective cutoff for `ty` from the resolved configuration, preserving package overrides and the existing global fallback for project and script checks. Fixes astral-sh/uv#21211.
signal.author: astral-automations-bot[bot]

signal.title: `uv check --script` ignores `exclude-newer-package` exemptions when selecting `ty`
signal.text: ### Summary ## Summary `uv check --script` applies the global `exclude-newer` cutoff when selecting ty, even when ty is explicitly exempted with `exclude-newer-package = { ty = false }`. ## Reproduction `pyproject.toml`: ```toml [project] name = "example" version = "0.1.0" requires-python = ">=3.12" [tool.uv] package = false exclude-newer = "P7D" exclude-newer-package = { ty = false } ``` `script.py`: ```python # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.12" # dependencies = [] # # [tool.uv] # exclude-newer = "P7D" # exclude-newer-package = { ty = false } # /// value: int = 1 ``` ```console $ uvx --no-config ty@latest --version ty 0.0.73 (4bd2833c4 2026-08-18) $ uv check --script script.py --show-version --preview-features=check-command Using ty 0.0.70 All checks passed! ``` ## Expected behavior `uv check --script` respects the ty-specific exemption and selects ty 0.0.73. ## Actual behavior `uv check --script` ignores the exemption and selects ty 0.0.70. ## Likely cause `crates/uv/src/commands/project/check.rs` passes only the global cutoff to the ty resolver: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/76d653943c6c82d3cca03227c24e98b1d0320aed/crates/uv/src/commands/project/check.rs#L721-L725 Package-specific overrides are discarded. ### Platform aarch64-apple-darwin ### Version uv 0.12.5 (210d1f678 2026-08-14) ### Python version _No response_
signal.author: AlexWaygood

signal.title: Reuse direct URL wheels across hash fragments
signal.text: Direct wheel requirements can include hash fragments, but lockfiles store the fragment-free URL. Using the original requirement URL as the wheel cache key can therefore prevent an offline sync from reusing an already-downloaded wheel. Use the fragment-free location for new cache entries and retain a fallback for older fragment-bearing entries. Check the expected hashes, size, and archive existence before reuse. When online, refresh a cached direct wheel if its contents no longer match the required hash or size, even when its HTTP response is still fresh. The regression tests cover offline reuse from lockfiles, offline hash mismatches, and changed contents at the same URL.
signal.author: konstin

signal.title: Cover recursive extras with mixed production markers
signal.text: Stacked on #21163; follow-up coverage for #21181. Extend the recursive-extra marker test with a dependency that is active either through a Python-version condition or through an extra. Check that recursive expansion retains only the additional environment activated by the extra, excluding the portion already required in production. This is a test-only change.
signal.author: konstin

signal.title: Allow an empty metadata cache when adding lower bounds
signal.text: Stacked on #21163. Reusing a metadata-free lock can leave the in-memory distribution index empty. When `uv add` inserts a lower bound and locks again, invalidating the project's metadata must tolerate an entry that was never cached. Remove the cache-presence assertion and extend the existing lower-bound regression test to cover adding a redundant marker after reusing a metadata-free lock.
signal.author: konstin

signal.title: Too strict PEP508 validation for URLs without file extension
signal.text: ### Summary Hi, package pyro-api contains following URL in test dependencies (extra_requires): ``` pyro-ppl@https://api.github.com/repos/pyro-ppl/pyro/tarball/dev ``` See https://github.com/pyro-ppl/pyro-api/blob/0.1.2/setup.py I know the comment in setup.py says to remove these lines before uploading to PyPI, however I don't think this comment is correct. The above URL is fine, can be downloaded (creates a tar.gz file) and satisfies the PEP508 grammar (I checked it using code like at https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/8326#issuecomment-2423123210_) Note: I don't want to discuss if it makes sense to provide a non-pinned, no-hash, mutable URL as a requirement. After building a wheel pyro-abi 0.1.2 directly from the source code (without commenting out the test extras), I can install the resulting wheel using 'pip'. However, installation with uv fails: ``` × Failed to read `pyro-api @ file:///tmp/pyro_api-0.1.2-py3-none-any.whl` ├─▶ Couldn't parse metadata of pyro_api-0.1.2-py3-none-any.whl from pyro-api @ file:///work/lbuild-out/pyro_api-0.1.2-py3-none-any.whl ╰─▶ Expected direct URL (`https://api.github.com/repos/pyro-ppl/pyro/tarball/dev`) to end in a supported file extension: `.whl`, `.tar.gz`, `.zip`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.lz`, `.tar.lzma`, `.tar.xz`, `.tar.zst`, `.tar`, `.tbz`, `.tgz`, `.tlz`, or `.txz` pyro-ppl@ https://api.github.com/repos/pyro-ppl/pyro/tarball/dev ; extra == "test" ``` I believe the requirement of the file extension is too strict and not justified by PEP508 (or PEP 440). My expectation is that `pyro-ppl@https://api.github.com/repos/pyro-ppl/pyro/tarball/dev` should be accepted as a proper requirement URL. ### Platform Linux 6.10.14-linuxkit aarch64 GNU/Linux ### Version uv 0.9.22 (82a6a66b8 2026-01-06) ### Python version 3.13.8

signal.title: Give automated bug fixes a writable Cargo cache
signal.text: Automated bug fixes cannot run Cargo tests when a missing crate must be downloaded because the default Cargo registry cache is read-only inside the Codex sandbox. Set `CARGO_HOME` to a writable runner temporary directory for the bug-fixing action so dependency downloads and targeted validation can complete.

signal.title: Promote ready uv-security pull requests
signal.text: Pull requests in `uv-security` currently have no promotion path when a maintainer marks them ready for review. Add the corresponding dispatcher route and a credential-broker grant scoped to `uv` and `uv-security`, while preserving the existing `uv-dev` authorization. Unlike `uv-dev`, the private repository is not part of uv's public fork network. Keep clean parent updates in a separate read-only job, then transfer the approved revision or verified candidate without checking it out in the publisher. Require the target base to already be public and recheck the source approval before creating the upstream branch. Retain the approved-revision and stacked-parent checks, and require the private PR's promoter to have repository write access.

signal.title: Index username stripped from url in `uv-receipt.toml` preventing tool upgrades
signal.text: ### Summary When you install a tool from a private index whose URL has a username value but no password in it, the resulting `uv-receipt.toml` has a stripped version of the URL without the username. This causes `uv tool upgrade <toolname>` to silently fail. You have to instead re-provide the index with the username like `uv tool upgrade <toolname> --index https://user@private.index/simple`. signal.title: Preserve transitive self-constraints in recursive extras
signal.text: uv currently loses recursive self-constraints: If `project[outer]` includes `project[middle]`, and the `middle` extra requires `project[inner]>=2`, uv must honor the `>=2` requirement and not accept `project==1`. To do this, we keep recursive requirement around instead of discarding it. Related to #21181.
signal.author: konstin

signal.title: Clarify no-build docs for editable requirements
signal.text: The `--no-build` help says resolving will not run arbitrary Python code and operations that require building distributions will fail. This conflicts with `docs/pip/compatibility.md` and the implementation: `--no-build` aliases `--only-binary :all:`, but uv may still build editable requirements under either option, and their build backends may execute arbitrary Python code. This PR updates the help text to align with reality and the doc mentioned above.
signal.author: zsol

signal.title: Make uv tool upgrade --all tolerant to deleted Python versions
signal.text: ### Summary This is partly a follow up to some of the commentary on https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/8067 I found if I deleted a uv python version (in this case because I'd installed Python 3.13.2 with uv), e.g. ```shell uv python uninstall cpython-3.13.1-windows-x86_64-none ``` and that was the Python my uv tools were installed against, when I run: ```shell uv tool upgrade --all ``` I get a long list of errors, e.g. ```shell error: Failed to upgrade hatch Caused by: `hatch` is missing a valid environment; run `uv tool install --force hatch` to reinstall error: Failed to upgrade linkchecker Caused by: `linkchecker` is missing a valid environment; run `uv tool install --force linkchecker` to reinstall error: Failed to upgrade maturin Caused by: `maturin` is missing a valid environment; run `uv tool install --force maturin` to reinstall error: Failed to upgrade mkdocs Caused by: `mkdocs` is missing a valid environment; run `uv tool install --force mkdocs` to reinstall ``` My only options (I'm aware of) to get around this are to: 1. For each tool call `uv tool install --force <tool name>` as suggested (but I have dozens of tools and that's onerous). 2. Reinstall the Python I deleted `uv python install cpython-3.13.1-windows-x86_64-none`, then run `uv tool upgrade --all --python 3.13.2`, then uninstall the older Python after the upgrade `uv python install cpython-3.13.1-windows-x86_64-none` - which is easy when you understand the workflow but not obvious and for me required searching uv documentation / issues I was hoping the behaviour of `uv tool upgrade --all` could be changed to do a force reinstall itself in the situation the previous Python it was installed against was removed - or there could be some new CLI options, e.g. `uv tool upgrade --all --force` or `uv tool reinstall --all` - something like that where I could express I do want to force reinstall everything in the case I know I have deleted the Python the tool was installed with. I guess a related bit of feature parity it'd be nice to have versus pipx is `pipx list` shows the Python version each package was installed with whereas `uv tool list` doesn't show that. My current uv version is: `uv 0.6.0 (591f38c25 2025-02-14)`
signal.author: owenlamont

signal.title: uv tool install: "--reinstall" option broken
signal.text: ### Summary `uv tool install --help` shows an option `--reinstall` to reinstall _all_ packages. However, this option requires a single package: ```bash ❯ uv tool install --help | grep -- --reinstall --reinstall Reinstall all packages, regardless of whether they're already installed. Implies `--refresh` --reinstall-package <REINSTALL_PACKAGE> Reinstall a specific package, regardless of whether it's already installed. Implies ❯ uv tool install --reinstall error: the following required arguments were not provided: <PACKAGE> Usage: uv.exe tool install --reinstall <PACKAGE> For more information, try '--help'. ``` Use case: trying to "fix" installation after removing the version of python they were installed with. (No warning or error was given during `uv python uninstall 3.13.2`.) See also #14814, which speaks to more of conflicting information about this use case. ### Platform Windows version: 10.0.26200.5722, arm64 ### Version uv 0.8.4 (e176e1714 2025-07-30) ### Python version ❯ uv python list | grep -v available > cpython-3.13.3-windows-aarch64-none C:\Users\hwine\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313-arm64\python.exe > cpython-3.10.16-windows-x86_64-none C:\Users\hwine\AppData\Roaming\uv\python\cpython-3.10.16-windows-x86_64-none\python.exe

signal.title: Alternatives for handling issues with `uv lock [--check]` and `exclude-newer`
signal.text: ### Summary We create the `uv.lock` files for our client projects on our Mac workstations. The projects run containerized in both dev and prod machines. We're planning on instituting a company-wide 7-day cooldown period in all of our global package manager configurations on our workstations. In preparation for this, I was experimenting with `exclude-newer` in my global `uv.toml`, but this caused a container build failure after a subsequent lockfile update. To ensure that the lockfile is up to date with `pyproject.toml` during the container build, in `Dockerfile`, we've got an early `uv lock --check` command (and a later install with `uv sync --locked`, ensuring no lockfile changes are attempted by the build process). If the lockfile check fails, we'll manually update it on the host and then retry the container build. The error in the build process is this: ``` $ uv lock --check Using CPython 3.14.3 interpreter at: /usr/local/bin/python3 Resolving despite existing lockfile due to removal of global exclude newer Resolved 70 packages in 1.64s The lockfile at `uv.lock` needs to be updated, but `--check` was provided. To update the lockfile, run `uv lock`. ``` The lockfile is up to date as far as the packages are concerned. Seemingly `--check` doesn't like these two lines that the host-level locking created, since the container doesn't have `exclude-newer` configured. ``` [options] exclude-newer = "2026-03-24T09:21:26.001329Z" exclude-newer-span = "P7D" ``` I guess the question is, is this `exclude-newer` configuration mismatch so serious that it should unconditionally fail the lockfile check? For us, it's certainly not. There are various ways to approach this, including but not limited to the following: - An option like `--check-packages-only` for `uv lock`, deliberately only caring about the locked packages matching `pyproject.toml`, not `exclude-newer` or other similar non-package-version-related mismatches. - A specific option for `--check` to ignore the `exclude-newer` mismatch. - No change; always require `exclude-newer` in `pyproject.toml` if host/container consistency is needed. ---- What to do when encountering an existing lockfile/config mismatch is one thing, but could this perhaps be caught earlier, at the time when the options would get baked into the lockfile in the first place? Consider this scenario: a project doesn't have `exclude-newer` in `pyproject.toml`, deliberately or not. A new contributor has `exclude-newer` globally set and runs `uv lock` to add a dependency, baking the options to the lockfile, possibly to the consternation of other developers down the line without `exclude-newer` set who have to deal with testing the PR or resultant CI failures if `uv lock --check` is involved. Perhaps a global-only config could be handled specially to avoid problems like this? If the lockfile doesn't already contain `exclude-newer` options AND the option is only set globally by the user running `uv lock`, not in `pyproject.toml` for the project being locked nor specified with `--exclude-newer[-package]`, pick one of these options: a) Warn the user, refuse to lock the file, require specifying an option that tells uv whether to bake the options in. b) Prompt the user about what to do, offering to lock with or without baking the options in. Likewise, if the lockfile already does contain `exclude-newer`, but `pyproject.toml` for some reason doesn't, it would probably be clearest to not change the baked-in values if they differ from the locking user's global setting only. I'm sure there are backwards compatibility considerations here, but I feel like uv needs a somewhat "clearer story" around globally set `exclude-newer`. With supply chain attacks happening regularly, articles around the web increasingly recommend global package manager configs for cooldowns, so the current behavior is bound to cause surprises for people down the line. ### Example _No response_

signal.title: `uv sync --frozen` ignores all index/mirror configuration and uses hardcoded URLs from `uv.lock`
signal.text: # Bug Report: `uv sync --frozen` ignores all index/mirror configuration and uses hardcoded URLs from `uv.lock` ## Environment - **uv version**: 0.11.14 (in Dify plugin daemon) & 0.11.17 (latest, locally tested) - **Platform**: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, x86_64) / macOS (Darwin 15.6.1, arm64) - **Python**: 3.12+ (tested with 3.12 and 3.13) ## Description When running `uv sync --frozen --no-dev`, **all index/mirror configuration methods are completely ignored**. uv downloads packages directly from the hardcoded URLs stored in `uv.lock` (typically `https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/...`), regardless of: - Command-line flag: `-i https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/` - Environment variable: `UV_INDEX_URL` - Environment variable: `UV_DEFAULT_INDEX` - Config file: `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` (`[[index]]` section) - Config file: `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` (`[pip]` section) - Project config: `pyproject.toml` (`[[tool.uv.index]]` section) **In contrast**, running `uv sync` **without** `--frozen` correctly respects the mirror configuration. This is a critical issue for users in regions where `files.pythonhosted.org` is slow or inaccessible (e.g., China), as well as for enterprise environments using private PyPI mirrors. ## Steps to Reproduce ```bash # 1. Create a test project mkdir -p /tmp/uv-frozen-bug && cd /tmp/uv-frozen-bug cat > pyproject.toml << 'EOF' [project] name = "frozen-mirror-test" version = "0.0.1" requires-python = ">=3.12" dependencies = [ "pydantic>=2.0", "requests>=2.31", "rich>=13.0", ] EOF # 2. Generate lockfile (this will use default pypi.org -> pythonhosted URLs) uv sync # 3. Verify uv.lock contains hardcoded pythonhosted URLs grep -c "files.pythonhosted.org" uv.lock # Output: 155 (or similar number of hardcoded URLs) # 4. Clean venv to force re-download rm -rf .venv # 5. Try frozen sync WITH mirror config (verbose to see actual URLs) UV_INDEX_URL=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/ \ uv sync --frozen --no-dev -v 2>&1 | grep -E "(aliyun|pythonhosted|Downloading)" # EXPECTED: Downloading from mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/... # ACTUAL: Downloading from files.pythonhosted.org/packages/c1/81/...pydantic_core... # Downloading from files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f4/7e/...pygments... # Downloading from files.pythonhosted.org/packages/82/3b/...rich... # 6. For comparison: try WITHOUT --frozen (same mirror config) rm -rf .venv UV_INDEX_URL=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/ \ uv sync --no-dev -v 2>&1 | grep -E "(aliyun|pythonhosted|Using index|Resolved)" # RESULT: Uses mirrors.aliyun.com correctly! ✅ ``` ## Expected Behavior `--frozen` should **freeze dependency versions** (which it does correctly), but should still use the configured **download source/index URL** for fetching packages. Version locking and download source are two separate concerns. Expected output: ``` Resolved from index at: https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/ Downloading https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/packages/...pydantic_core... ``` ## Actual Behavior ``` # All 7 configuration methods are ignored: DEBUG Resolved 155 packages in Xms Downloading https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/c1/81/...pydantic_core-2.30.0-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.manylinux2014_x86_64.whl Downloading https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f4/7e/...pygments-2.19.0-py3-none-any.whl Downloading https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/82/3b/...rich-13.9.4-py3-none-any.whl # ... all from pythonhosted, completely ignoring UV_INDEX_URL ``` ## Comparison Table | Mode | Mirror Config Set | Actual Download Source | Result | |------|-------------------|----------------------|--------| | `uv sync --no-dev` | `UV_INDEX_URL=aliyun` | `mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/...` | ✅ Works | | `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` | `UV_INDEX_URL=aliyun` | `files.pythonhosted.org/packages/...` | ❌ Ignored | ## Real-World Impact This bug caused **6 failed installation attempts** of a Python plugin in our production environment (Dify AI platform on a 2C4G cloud server in China): 1. Plugin daemon calls `uv sync --no-dev --frozen` internally 2. All dependencies download from `files.pythonhosted.org` at ~10 KB/s (vs ~10 MB/s from Chinese mirrors) 3. Download timeout after 300s → `signal: terminated` → installation failure 4. Server has limited RAM (4GB) + swap, so slow downloads also risk OOM during dependency building **Workaround used**: Replaced `/usr/local/bin/uv` with a bash wrapper that intercepts `uv sync` calls and redirects them to `pip3 install -i <mirror-url>`. ```bash #!/bin/bash # /usr/local/bin/uv (wrapper script) if [[ "$1" == "sync" ]]; then echo "[wrapper] Intercepted uv sync -> using pip3 with aliyun mirror" >&2 # Create venv with pip, install deps via pip3 -i <mirror> python3 -m venv .venv DEPS=$(python3 -c "import tomllib; ...") echo "$DEPS" | .venv/bin/pip3 install -i "$INDEX_URL" -r /dev/stdin exit $? else exec /usr/local/bin/uv-real "$@" fi ``` ## Suggested Fix Direction The `--frozen` flag's purpose is to **lock dependency versions**, not to **lock download URLs**. The fix should: 1. Read package versions and hashes from `uv.lock` (current behavior — correct) 2. Resolve the **actual download URL** using the configured index/mirror (new behavior) 3. Only fall back to the lockfile's hardcoded URL if the configured index doesn't have the matching package+version+hash This is similar to how Cargo/Rust handles `.lock` files: versions are locked, but registries can be configured independently. ## Related Issues - **#6349** — Feature request for `uv.lock` to support different index URLs across machines/CI environments. This bug is essentially the **runtime manifestation** of that design limitation. - **#16996** — `--frozen` silently ignores resolution options (different scope, same pattern of silent ignoring) ## Additional Notes - The `uv.lock` format stores per-package download URLs like: ```toml wheels = [{ url = "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/...", hash = "sha256:..." }] ``` These URLs are resolved at lockfile generation time and baked in permanently. - In `--frozen` mode, uv appears to use these stored URLs directly without consulting any runtime index configuration. - Tested on both **0.11.14** (Dify's pinned version) and **0.11.17** (latest release as of 2025-05-28). Behavior is identical — this is not version-specific.
signal.author: chenshengtao666

signal.title: `uv run` uses wrong python interpreter inside virtualenv with copied python
signal.text: ### Summary I tried using uv with an old project that creates its own venv using a python version that isn't the system deafult python. The system default /usr/bin/python3, used by default by uv, is python3.9 ```sh % uv run python --version Python 3.9.25 ``` `uv run --with some_dependency` breaks inside venvs that use a different python. Minimal reproduction: ```sh % cd `mktemp -d` % python3.13 <<< 'import venv ; venv.create(".venv")' % . .venv/bin/activate % uv run --with ipython ipython Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/mneergaa/.cache/uv/builds-v0/.tmpfB0eqd/bin/ipython", line 4, in <module> from IPython import start_ipython ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'IPython' ``` Interestingly, it works if I use `python3 -m venv` to create the venv, probably because that uses symlinks instead of copying: ```sh % cd `mktemp -d` % python3.13 -m venv .venv % . .venv/bin/activate % uv run --with ipython ipython Python 3.13.14 (main, Jun 11 2026, 00:00:00) [GCC 11.5.0 20240719 (Red Hat 11.5.0-14)] [...] ``` ### Platform CentOS Stream release 9 ### Version uv 0.12.2 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) ### Python version Python 3.9.25 / Python 3.13.14
signal.author: xim

signal.title: Lock Prettier tooling and disable install scripts
signal.text: The formatting workflow, contributor commands, generators, and editor hook fetch Prettier through one-shot `npx` invocations without a committed lockfile. Add a shared private `npm` toolchain that locks the existing `3.9.0` formatter and the README generator's `3.8.3` release, and disable lifecycle scripts in `.npmrc`. Require `npm>=11.10.0` through `engines.npm` and `engine-strict` so older installers cannot silently ignore the seven-day `min-release-age` policy for new resolutions. CI pins Node.js to `24.19.0`, and CI and release preparation install the tools with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. Callers then run the installed CLI directly so formatting cannot fall back to a download. Keep the root tooling lock under Renovate's shared update policy. Related: astral-sh/uv#21197 removes uv's contributor hook configuration. astral-sh/uv#21204 separately moves Python-tool invocations into the locked `check` group. astral-sh/ruff#27842 hardens the native `prek` formatter environment, while astral-sh/hawk#161 records a locked `npm` formatter environment.

signal.title: Only warn about unbounded build backends for source distributions
signal.text: An unbounded `uv_build` requirement currently triggers a warning while building wheels, editable wheels, and metadata even though those artifacts do not distribute build-system requirements. Restrict the missing-upper-bound warning to source-distribution build. I think our warning here is a bit overzealous for people who do not intend to distribute a source distribution, so I think we should scope the warning to the case we're focused on. For example, `uv sync` and `uv build --wheel` will no longer emit the warning. Closes astral-sh/uv#21074
signal.author: astral-automations-bot[bot]

signal.title: uv-build: suppress "missing upper bound" warning via env var
signal.text: ### Summary I frequently work with Python projects where uv is locked by [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/). A dummy project with mise + uv + configuration scaffolding is [here](https://github.com/manselmi/yospos). Given that 1. [mise locks the uv version](https://github.com/manselmi/yospos/blob/019a251385da23e3ad74254141e156d627ae4074/mise.lock#L22-L42), and 2. given my understanding (which might very well be wrong) that commands such as `uv build` and `uv sync` use a build backend embedded in the `uv` binary, which I assume doesn't need to download the `uv-build` Python package (again, this might be wrong), it seems like it should be safe to omit an upper bound (or any sort of version constraint) for `uv-build` in `build-system.requires` in `pyproject.toml` ([example](https://github.com/manselmi/yospos/blob/019a251385da23e3ad74254141e156d627ae4074/pyproject.toml#L8)). However, as far as I know, there is no way to suppress the following warning without specifying an upper bound on `uv-build`: ``` text warning: `build_system.requires = ["uv-build"]` is missing an upper bound on the `uv_build` version such as `<0.13`. Without bounding the `uv_build` version, the source distribution will break when a future, breaking version of `uv_build` is released. ``` I would like to be able to suppress this warning, perhaps via environment variable, in situations where uv is pinned. If uv is pinned then the warning is effectively a false-positive, and the alert should be suppressible to reduce alert fatigue. Also, in this situation it makes sense to specify a `uv`/`uv-build` version constraint in only one place, `mise.toml`, and not in both `mise.toml` and `pyproject.toml`, yet another reason for making the warning suppressible. ``` console % uv --version uv 0.12.3 (Homebrew 2026-08-07 aarch64-apple-darwin) ``` ### Example #### Current behavior Warning emitted, as there's no way to suppress the `uv-build` upper bound warning without supplying an upper bound. First, clone https://github.com/manselmi/yospos/ then run ``` console % mise exec -- uv build --wheel Building wheel... warning: `build_system.requires = ["uv-build"]` is missing an upper bound on the `uv_build` version such as `<0.13`. Without bounding the `uv_build` version, the source distribution will break when a future, breaking version of `uv_build` is released. ``` (The example project only supports Linux and macOS but you get the idea.) #### Desired behavior Warning suppressed when some environment variable is truthy. `UV_NO_BUILD_UPPER_BOUND_WARNING` is used in the following example, although that's a mouthful. ``` console % env -- UV_NO_BUILD_UPPER_BOUND_WARNING=1 mise exec -- uv build --wheel Building wheel... ``` In practice, this environment variable would be set in a project-specific `mise.toml` configuration file so that it doesn't need to be manually set.
signal.author: manselmi
